executionAuthorization.scope: This static plan authorizes no optimizer call. Root must separately approve frozen source and an isolated first-run timing window.

hypothesis: Under these two already-seen original V12 prefixes, replacing the audited D5 native endpoint with its already-produced audited seed may avoid the documented next-day mandatory warehouse conflict. M is only a necessary-load proxy, not a recovery guarantee.
selectionRule: Screen every D5 preceding the 14 pressure loss-union episodes (five business scenarios). Eligible only when the original timely audited seed existed, native was selected for strictly lower current fees, and native next-day mandatory warehouse M strictly exceeded seed M. All six eligible original episodes are retained as references and deduplicated by public input/prefix/two-endpoint identity into the two cases below.

deduplication.canonicalRule: Use the smallest original repeatIndex, a1, only after all three original identities match. Timing metadata is preserved in original raw files, not asserted byte-identical.

cases.sourceMultiplicityScope: Three original clock/algorithm repeats have identical public input, physical prefix and both endpoints. They are one business-case endpoint pair, not three independent samples.

timingRepetitionScope: Three fresh cold clock repetitions of each fixed case/branch. The old algorithm seed stays69011 and native RNG stays0; these are not new orders, independent business cases, a new algorithm seed or confidence-interval samples.

hashContract.canonicalization: Recursively sort object keys by JavaScript Object.keys(x).sort(), JSON.stringify keys/primitives with no whitespace, arrays retain source order; no undefined or non-finite values. Dates retain original container order.

executionOrder: Jobs array is authoritative. Pair adjacent branches within a case; alternate case order across timing repeats and branch order by (timingRepeatIndex + canonical case index) parity. Serial execution, no concurrent native/timed work.

physicalReplay.daysZeroThroughFour: Return the original canonical V12 timeline complete decisions, freshly rowFor-priced and audited under each replayed public snapshot. Verify every prefix projection and observation hash.
physicalReplay.dayFive: Use exactly the selected archived seed/native endpoint. Both see the same public snapshot and locks. Reprice/audit, then explicitly import only those dates into a fresh replay-enabled V13 cache; this is forced intervention, not a natural V13/native solution discovery.
physicalReplay.daySixOnward: Both branches use the same frozen V13 native policy with current public observations and their own actually executed locks. Real future capacity is revealed only by the unchanged daily simulator.
physicalReplay.sourceActualFutureAccess: Only the simulator may read original private events/durations. No such list, future realization, oracle capacity or case-specific recovery hint enters the planner or import API.

developmentImport.clock: Factory clock only, default performance.now; import and forced D5 audit share the same absolute deadline. No call-site replacement clock.
audit: Exact historical locks and no unexecuted event in past
Deadline check after all audit/selection work before cache commit
developmentImport.receipt: Preserve accepted/rejected status, absolute start/deadline, each phase timestamp, snapshot/locks/source dates/canonical rows/fees and audit. Bind their canonical SHA values. No mutable cache references.
developmentImport.failure: Retain the rejected import/forced-decision receipt and fail that branch. No retry, fake native priming, extra allowance or invisible cache write.
developmentImport.nextDecision: D6 reaudits the imported cache normally under the new public snapshot and actual history.
chargedToColdBudget: D5 endpoint audits and cache import

scopeLimits: This is one fixed-prefix intervention study on two selected seen cases, not a new holdout, full-D0 V13 policy evaluation, natural policy counterfactual, average causal effect or ranking proof.

A full candidate valid under the current public capacities remains a witness after its own today actions are frozen, so ordinary necessary-condition feasibility checks cannot reject it without a new declared assumption. The M comparison is a heuristic resource-exposure ordering.
M(seed) below M(native) is not joint recoverability. Transport/staging/cross-day coupling and subsequent new shocks can defeat both branches.
The two original D0 losses, the remaining eight pressure certificate episodes, and the three same-distribution D4 counterexamples are not claimed fixed by this local D5 guard.
The native endpoint saves current model fees in both selected cases. Keeping the seed can raise fees; report that tradeoff rather than promise simultaneous completion/fee/churn improvement.

reporting.unit: two unique business cases, with three timing repetitions per fixed case/branch
reporting.comparisons: Paired branch completion/failure day/status first; fees and revisions only within jointly completed matching timing pairs, with distinct denominators. No zero fee imputation for failed paths.
reporting.acceptance: A complete result requires all original V12 cold lifecycle gates, not just a timely terminal message or a complete static plan.
reporting.timing: D0-D5 optimization is intentionally replaced by archived endpoints. Whole-branch time is not full-D0 V13 runtime.

stoppingRule: Run the exact twelve jobs once after root authorization. Finish the declared matrix even when early jobs fail; no rerun, parameter tuning, widened budget, post-outcome case exclusion, new timing repeat or sample expansion. Harness errors retain the original failed attempt and require a separately declared corrected attempt before any rerun.
